Recognizable mature date palm (Phoenix dactylifera) at established catalogue rendering quality, not photorealism. Whole: a single unbranched trunk carrying a rosette of arching pinnate fronds at the apex, the lower fronds drooping below the crown base, no branches, no foliage on the trunk. Trunk: the trunk clothed in retained leaf bases in a spiral from the crown down (not yet expressed by the generator; assess what is drawn, never invent it). Base: the leaf-base pattern at close range (same caveat). Photographs establish species character; the independent spruce anchor establishes finish quality only, never morphology. Additional realism optional. Unassessable cells unknown.
Authoritative owner requirements: Second revision (2026-09-23): the trunk organs (fn-110) are landed and in the dial table; dial ranges come from validated bounds (fn-113) and strides from the named gap (fn-114). The date cluster (fn-111) is not landed. Priorities in the owner's words: the crown must read as a palm's rosette of long arching pinnate fronds with the lowest fronds drooping; the fronds are far too thin and short today (leaflet size and frond length are the first dials); the trunk must be straight or gently leaning, never wavy, of near-constant diameter; nothing grows on the trunk. Reviewer: Opus (claude) through the Claude adapter twins, the owner's fallback of 2026-09-22 while the Codex-backed Astra reviewer is out of quota; uncalibrated on this model. Dial table: `spacing` (short-shoot spacing, the palm bears no short shoots, value 0) and `taper` (twig tip taper, the palm's 1.0 is outside the authored 0.05-0.6 and is where the owner wants the trunk) are left out because their current palm values fall outside their authored ranges (host, 2026-09-22).

observations: Three references are treated as independent specimens; no assumption is made that any two show the same individual or a change over time.
reference-0 is a distant full-tree view at low sun with strong colour grading; fine trunk and leaflet detail is not resolvable there and is only inferred at silhouette level.
reference-1 and reference-2 are close views of the mid-trunk and lower crown; neither shows the tree base or the whole crown outline, and neither shows fruit.
No reference shows the ground-level root zone in detail, flowers/inflorescences at anthesis, offshoots or suckers, or the underside of a frond in detail; these remain unobserved rather than absent.
Fruit colour (orange to orange-red) is observed only in reference-0 and represents a single maturity state; other ripeness colours are not evidenced here.

The foliage colour difference between references (deep green vs. grey-glaucous) is recorded as an observation; lighting, processing, maturity, and taxon/cultivar identity are all candidate causes and none is established by the images.
Epiphytic ferns and vines on the trunk are observed features of the scene in reference-1/2, not necessarily characteristic of the species.
Background context differs (waterside rice fields and village in reference-0; mown turf and broadleaf trees in reference-1/2) and carries no weight for morphology.
Neighbouring palms are partly visible at the frame edges of reference-1 and reference-2; traits were read from the central subject only.
No photorealism or pixel-level correspondence is required or claimed; traits are described at the level of recognisable structure.

traits.observation: Crown composed of many long once-pinnate (feather) fronds radiating from a single apical point, each frond arching outward and downward so the outline of the crown reads as a rounded hemisphere to shuttlecock shape; frond count per crown appears high (roughly 30-60 visible), with the newest fronds held stiffly upward near the center and older ones progressively more recurved.

Leaflets are narrow, stiff, linear-lanceolate and taper to sharp points; they are inserted along the rachis in groups and at differing angles so the frond has a plumose/V-sectioned look rather than a flat plane. Leaflet tips appear rigid and spreading, giving the frond margin a bristly silhouette.

Trunk surface is covered in persistent cut or broken leaf-base stubs arranged in a spiral, tessellating into a diamond/rhomboid lattice; each stub is a blunt wedge projecting several centimetres from the trunk with a flat, angular outer face. The pattern is coarse and irregular in reference-1/2 and reads as a finer knobbly texture at distance in reference-0.
Between and behind the leaf-base stubs the trunk is packed with coarse reddish-brown fibre and shredded husk, forming a shaggy matted layer that fills the interstices of the diamond lattice.
A single unbranched columnar stem of roughly constant diameter carries the crown; no branching is visible anywhere along the stem in any reference.

Heavy pendent fruiting bunches hang from below the crown on thick stalks that emerge among the frond bases and bend downward; the fruit mass is dense, composed of many small ellipsoid fruits, and coloured saturated orange to orange-red. Two to three such bunches are visible on one crown.

Beneath the living crown hangs a collar of dead and dying fronds, brown to grey, collapsed downward against the upper trunk and partly obscuring it; the transition from green living fronds to brown dead fronds is abrupt in reference-0.

Foliage colour differs across the references: deep saturated green in reference-0 versus a pale grey-green to blue-glaucous cast in reference-1 and reference-2. Both appear as plausible foliage states; lighting (overcast sunset vs. direct midday sun) and possible cultivar or taxon difference are separate candidate causes and cannot be distinguished from the images.
At the crown apex the emerging leaf bases show pale green to yellow-green petioles with patches of rust-orange fibrous sheath material and reddish-brown tones where the bases are cut or broken.

Trunk posture varies: strongly leaning and S-curved, meeting the ground at a pronounced angle with a swollen curved basal region in reference-0, versus essentially vertical and straight in reference-1 and reference-2. Both are within the visible range for this form.

Bright yellow-green ferns with narrow pinnate fronds grow out of the leaf-base pockets over a wide band of the trunk, rooted in the fibrous matting; also small vines/seedlings lower down. Present in reference-1 and reference-2 only, absent in reference-0.

Trunk colour ranges from mid grey-brown to warm reddish-brown; stub faces are lighter and greyer than the surrounding fibre, some bleached to pale grey, consistent with weathered exposed surfaces. Lower trunk in reference-0 reads more uniformly grey-brown with a finer texture than the coarse stubs shown close up.
Where the trunk meets the ground in reference-0 it widens into a broad rooted base merging into the soil mound; no clear detail of root boss or offshoots is resolvable at this scale.
No smooth green crownshaft is visible; living frond bases sit directly on the stub-covered trunk with no clean columnar sheath between crown and trunk.

Near the proximal end of the fronds the leaflets appear reduced to stiff, isolated, spine-like structures spaced along the petiole, though resolution limits confident separation of true spines from short rigid leaflets.

Crown diameter is large relative to trunk diameter (crown spread appears several times the trunk width) and the frond length is a substantial fraction of the visible trunk length in reference-0; exact ratios vary with viewing distance and cannot be measured reliably.
